As I said in the review on the first game, this one is amazing. Adds more characters, more story, and then... just when you think "oh it's silly", they hit you AGAIN. And you meet The King.

The sequel, but [i]also[/i] a parallel universe(??), to the first game! This one seemed to focus more on the Holiday aspect. However, I prefer the first game, for a few reasons, but you can read my review of the game [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/GizmoHaruhi/recommended/310080/]here![/url] 

I didn’t like this sequel as much, mainly because it is [b]much much[/b] shorter than the first game. I completed this in under 2 hours, it took an hour to get through the four Episodes, whereas the first game took me over 4 hours, almost 5 hours if I remember correctly. But also, because there was a lack of dialogue choices, and choosing what class to study, I wish we had seen something much similar to that, where it explores how we can interact with a certain bird in a day, or in an episode, which is the charm that Holiday Star was missing. I had lost interest within the game, like after the First Episode, whereas the first game had me hooked immediately, but I still managed to power through it. And I’ll still gladly say Sakuya is still my favourite character! But Nageki is getting a very close first, but just under Sakuya, I loved how they explored him in this one!

I also [b]LOVED LOVED!![/b] ([i]Keyword[/i], loved, right here) The upgraded human designs for each character, I think my jaw was on the floor when I saw Sakuya's human design. He definitely had a glow up in this game, and I loved seeing that quite a lot! ♡ 

I feel this wasn’t as polished, and as interesting, as the first game was, this was more episodic, and of course, you can easily fail the game/get a “Game Over”, I got that in the Second Episode. But it took ages to get to where I failed originally, because the “Fast Forward” button wasn’t as fast as the first game was. I did like the Episodic moments, and going back to the episodes to see the bad endings, but I didn’t like the ideology of continuously putting the name in per Episode, as in the first game, you’re just the name you’ve given the main character ([b]if[/b] you’ve changed it from [u]Hiyoko Tosaka[/u]), I do know as well that the original version of Hatoful Boyfriend had “Game Overs”, but they decided to remove that from the current version that we currently have. 

I did notice as well, how the BBL ending wasn’t continued in Holiday Star, and how all the characters were living a normal life, and just being oblivious. And I still had some questions that I needed an answer from from the BBL ending, and Holiday Star didn’t seem to give that to me. However, there was some foreshadowing (I love those!!!) in a storyline which also introduced some new characters; [b]The Day the Night Slept[/b]. So, I think people will like that storyline, I, myself for certain did!

I’ll still, however, recommend this game, to those who did enjoy the first game, and are Hatoful fans, like myself. But if you’re someone who is looking for a long-ish storyline, unfortunately you may not find yourself liking this one, but I’d personally say get it on sale, and who knows? It may be worth it for you! <3

I genuinely feel like they're tackling more difficult issues and yet the writing style seems more beautiful than the previous game. We learn more about the backstories of the birds, as well as their motivations and fears. The art is PHENOMENAL. I immediately bought the collector edition because I simply adored the backgrounds that are in the game.

For Nageki lovers, rejoice. He takes a bigger role in this game and I can say I sobbed really hard at a few moments.

I don't want to spoil anything because I truly believe the best way to experience this game is go into it blind, but it always fascinates me how Hatomoa can write such bittersweet stories that always hit me right in the heart.

In conclusion, this game didn't disappoint at all when compared to the first game. I love the Hatoful Boyfriend series so much and I truly hope more people can love it too.

It's been nearly 10 years since I've played this game for the first time, and it still hits just as hard as it did the first time I played it.

Holiday Star is set during christmas, in a parallell universe to the original game where certain events have not happened and certain rules do not apply. You absolutely need to have played the original to understand what is going on. The game has very few choices and you largely just follow the story (there are eight choices in total, very few). The story starts very silly but later becomes quite serious, something I found problematic in the original. The game can not decide whether or not it wants to be silly or serious and that gives it a sense of lacking identity. This did not speak to me and I do not recommend it. There are some graphical issues as well, with text overflowing from textboxes at times.

Play a more polished game, avoid this one.

Les pigeons les plus loufoques du Japon sont de retour pour fêter les fêtes de fin d'année !
Pour ce second épisode, nos héros vont faire de nombreuses enquêtes absurdes jusqu'à une conclusion qui n'a tout simplement aucun sens XD. Après, c'est ce qui avait fait le charme d'Hatoful Boyfriend ... Donc, avant de jouer, déconnectez votre cerveau !

Petite déception quand même sur les mini-histoires que l'on débloque qui ne sont pas particulièrement intéressante à lire. Après, malgré son univers WTF, il reste un visual novel riche mais classique donc si vous aimez ce style de jeu, aller vous faire pousser des ailes et voler en leurs compagnies !
